summary: go-server's Redis client timeouts were slashed to 1 millisecond (REDIS_READ_TIMEOUT_MS=1, REDIS_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS=1, REDIS_DIAL_TIMEOUT_MS=1), while go-enricher - which talks to the same Redis cluster - has these unset (library defaults, normally hundreds of ms+), so this is a single-service misconfiguration, not a stack-wide policy. Change CHG-909e1848 was injected, go-server was recreated 33 seconds later to pick up the new env vars, and on boot its Redis cluster client immediately hit an i/o timeout fetching COMMAND INFO from a cluster node. Since restart, throughput has stayed steady (~4/sec) and error counters haven't ticked up because most calls are sneaking in under 1ms on this fast local network, but there is zero margin - any GC pause or load bump would push real calls over the threshold, with failures landing on the dedup check (risk of duplicate fraud transactions slipping through or being spuriously errored). Redis cluster itself is healthy (3/3 nodes, 0 failed/pfail slots, stable memory), Kafka consumer lag is flat, and go-enricher's/redis1's/redis2's earlier restarts predate this injection and are unrelated leftover history. Fix: restore REDIS_READ_TIMEOUT_MS/REDIS_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS/REDIS_DIAL_TIMEOUT_MS on go-server to sane values.
